reason: Gravitational focusing should help rocky planetesimals collide and grow into an embryo.
expectation: The planetesimals will begin accumulating into a larger rocky body.

effect: Crossing orbits, rather than gravitational focusing directly, produced accreting embryos; I can now try adding water-bearing material.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified how growth starts.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock is a plausible way to supply the growing Earth with volatiles.
expectation: The embryos will incorporate hydrated rock, contributing to a volatile-bearing young Earth.

effect: The embryos cannot yet take up water-bearing rock; their available partners suggest further growth first.
reaction: The compatibility feedback clarified the next stage.
reason: Gravitational focusing should help the embryos gather more material and grow.
expectation: The embryos will grow into larger rocky bodies.

alternatives.reason: The listed planetesimals could also supply material for growth.

effect: Gravitational focusing produced a strongly attracting embryo, suggesting it can now gather more material.
reaction: The growth sequence is clearer now.
reason: The embryo's stronger attraction should help it accrete rocky planetesimals.
expectation: The embryo will grow into a larger rocky world.

alternatives.reason: It might instead gather volatile-bearing material at this stage.

effect: The embryo gathered rocky fragments and became a proto-Earth, which can now plausibly incorporate hydrated material.
reaction: The automatic pairing clarified which debris advances Earth’s growth.
reason: Water-bearing asteroid rock could supply the proto-Earth with volatiles.
expectation: The proto-Earth will incorporate hydrated rock and become volatile-bearing.

effect: Proto-Earth has incorporated hydrated rock, but that alone does not imply a cool surface or an ocean.
reaction: The distinction between hydrated material and a surface ocean is useful.
reason: Collisions could break the layered planetesimal and expose metal-bearing fragments for further accretion.
expectation: The collision will produce fragments from the planetesimal’s interior.

effect: The collision exposed metal-rich asteroid-core fragments that may contribute to proto-Earth’s growth.
reaction: The connection to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: The hydrated proto-Earth can plausibly accrete the newly exposed metal fragments.
expectation: The fragments will add metal to the growing, volatile-bearing Earth.

effect: The hydrated proto-Earth gathered metal fragments, completing the volatile-bearing Earth goal; another rocky embryo remains to be grown.
reaction: The overlapping arrival of metal and hydrated rock makes the growth sequence less rigid than I expected.
reason: Rocky planetesimals were listed as a compatible partner for the accreting embryos and could help grow another embryo.
expectation: The embryos will gather rocky material, producing another growing rocky body.

effect: The remaining planetesimals formed the hypothetical embryo Theia, completing the second goal and the chapter.
reaction: Theia’s uncertain size and composition make the impact scenario more tentative than a simple named-body story suggests.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding hydrated rock to proto-Earth was most worthwhile: it clarified that hydrogen-bearing material can join a hot growing planet without implying a surface ocean.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying hydrated rock on the embryos before they were ready was the least productive passage, although the compatibility feedback showed what growth options remained.

surprise.text: I was surprised that hydrated rock and metal could arrive in overlapping periods rather than in a fixed metal-first sequence.

arbitrary.text: The strongly attracting embryo accepting rocky-layer fragments rather than planetesimals felt somewhat specific; the feedback identified the required pairing, but I could not infer why the other rocky material would not work.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the hypothetical Theia encounter develops, especially given the uncertainty around the impactor.
